issues.text: The diagram reads left to right, and the parent/child chain continues to the right of 'paint', so 'parent sets the child's position' appears after paint. The prose says paint comes last. The prose also calls the chain 'the lower row', but with LR I am not sure which row is lower. I can narrate it only because the prose fixes the order.
issues.quote:
L --> P[paint: pixels drawn]
  L --> PA[parent passes constraints down]
issues.fix: Draw the arrow to paint from the last step of the chain (PO --> P) instead of from L, so the chain sits between layout and paint; or drop 'the lower row of' from the prose.

issues.text: Misconception 1 still gives the reason 'layout only matters visually anyway'. Everything in this lesson is visual, so I cannot picture who would reason this way; the belief 'they are one step' alone is plausible.
issues.quote: "Layout and paint are the same step, since layout only matters visually anyway."
issues.fix: Replace the reason with one a beginner would give, e.g. 'since Flutter can work out where a widget goes at the moment it draws it'; update the q5 statement and misconception to match.

issues.text: Inside the layout-vs-paint rebuttal, one sentence is about build vs layout ('what the widgets describe'). I stopped to work out how it shows layout and paint differ; it does not, it answers a different question.
issues.quote: Resizing the window changes where things go without changing what the widgets describe.
issues.fix: Delete this sentence; the next sentence (spinner moves, layout decides before paint draws) already makes the point.
